newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr to consolidate in quiet Asian trade.
newsitem.headline: Dlr to consolidate in quiet Asian trade.

text.p: The dollar is expected to consolidate in a tight range during Asian trading time on Thursday, with trade mostly quiet and dominated by position-adjustment by interbank traders, dealers said.
Its topside is seen heavy near 116.50 yen amid a lack of fresh buying impetus and steady exporter offers near 117 yen.
"As it was seen in New York, 116.50 yen remains very heavy," a city bank dealer said. The dollar was traded in a narrow range of 116.01 yen to 116.50 yen in New York.
Mark purchases for yen in cross trade may emerge after repeatedly failing to dip below 67 yen, dealers said.

"Some buying back of marks has already been detected. After it repeatedly failed to test the 66 yen level, mark purchases for yen may start," the city bank dealer said, adding such moves in crosses may be a key to subdued dollar/yen trade.
A trust bank dealer said importers may start buying dollars on dips below 116 yen, along with short-covering interest by interbank dealers, keeping the dollar's downside solid.
He added that some trust banks were said to be keen to buy dollars for yen as well. But he was not sure those bids are related to fresh foreign investment by pension funds.

On Wednesday, banking sources in Tokyo said that about 300 billion yen in fresh pension money was likely to be invested via trust banks in foreign assets, such as stocks and bonds, by the middle of this month.

Overnight, comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that he favours a strong mark in the future supported the mark against the dollar, but a surprisingly sharp 1.3 percent drop in German industrial output for the month of April weighed on the German currency.
But dealers said the impact from these factors on the German currency will be limited in Asia.
